title: Product Designer
description:
You'll own features end to end, from a fuzzy concept to a shipped, polished experience, and you'll design the interaction paradigms for a product where AI is the medium, not a feature bolted on. This is a hands-on generalist role with a high degree of autonomy and a high bar for craft.

It's deliberately not built for hyper-specialists or managers. At Luma, AI is how the work gets done: you're expected to think, generate, prototype, and build with it, using AI coding tools to make real working features rather than static mockups. It fits someone who has already changed how they design around AI and can move fast through ambiguity. If you need clear direction handed to you or prefer to stay in mockups, this won't suit.

What You'll Own



- Lead major features end to end, from product thinking and user exploration to pixel-perfect visual design and high-fidelity interactive prototypes.
- Design and prototype fluid, novel interactions for a new medium, making complex AI concepts feel intuitive.
- Build functional prototypes and shippable features using AI coding tools, in close partnership with engineering.
- Hold an exceptionally high bar for craft across visual design, interaction, and prototyping.
- Drive work forward through ambiguity: step into problems early, decide with incomplete information, and keep momentum.
- Collaborate with engineers, product, and AI researchers to shape strategy and ship the design vision at quality.

First 90 Days

One way the first 90 could unfold.



- Days 1–30 — Immerse & Diagnose: Learn the product and its AI-native interactions, and identify where the experience can be sharper.
- Days 30–60 — Ship & Validate: Own a real feature from concept to shipped, prototyped and built with AI tooling alongside engineering.
- Days 60–90 — Scale & Systemize: Raise the craft bar around you and set patterns other designers and engineers can build on.

What You Bring



- 5+ years building delightful, innovative products at scale.
- Strength in both craft and product thinking, across visual and interaction design.
- AI woven visibly into your process and portfolio, with experience building functional prototypes in tools like Cursor or Claude Code.
- A portfolio of work that shipped to production, showing how you framed the problem, how it evolved, and its impact.
- Comfort moving fast, converging, and knowing when to stop iterating.
- A track record of creating momentum and influencing decisions across teams.
- A portfolio is required.

Nice to Have



- Experience designing complex creative software: video or photo editors, design tools, or developer tools.
- World-class interaction design: fluid micro-interactions, complex state transitions, prototypes well beyond static screens.

We're Fiserv, a global leader in Fintech and payments, and we move money and information in a way that moves the world. We connect financial institutions, corporations, merchants and consumers to one another millions of times a day - quickly, reliably, and securely. Any time you swipe your credit card, pay through a mobile app, or withdraw money from the bank, we're involved. If you want to make an impact on a global scale, come make a difference at Fiserv.

Job Title

Product Designer

About Clover

At Clover, we are committed to providing small businesses the tools, technology, and support they need to succeed and grow. Our solutions let you accept payments, run your business, and sell more. As part of Fiserv, we come from a larger team of problem solvers that serve millions of businesses worldwide. That means that our Clover customers benefit from a wealth of experience, technology and industry expertise.

What does a Product Designer do at Clover?

As a Product Designer within the Clover Design team at Fiserv, you’ll have a direct hand in enhancing the digital experience for our merchants and their customers by creating intuitive, human-centered designs across various products and platforms. This position offers an exciting opportunity to collaborate with cross-functional teams and contribute to the overall product strategy and user experience.

You will work closely with fellow designers, researchers, product managers, developers, and other stakeholders to ensure that design solutions align with business goals and technical feasibility. You will apply best practices and systems thinking to drive innovation and growth for small and medium businesses and enterprises.

Research and Testing

- Analyze test results to make data-driven recommendations for design improvements.

Product Design and UX

- Collaborate with the Director of Product Design and other team members to iterate on designs based on feedback and usability testing results.
- Maintain comprehensive design documentation, including annotated design specifications, journeys, product maps, and user flows to ensure clarity and consistency across projects.

title: Product Designer, Creator Success
description:
Patreon is a media and community platform where over 300,000 creators give their biggest fans access to exclusive work and experiences. We offer creators a variety of ways to engage with their fans and build a lasting business including: paid memberships, free memberships, community chats, live video, and selling to fans directly with one-time purchases.

Ultimately our goal is simple: fund the creative class. And we're leaders in that space, with:




- $10 billion+ generated by creators since Patreon's inception
- 100 million+ free memberships for fans who may not be ready to pay just yet, and
- 25 million+ paid memberships on Patreon today.


We're continuing to invest heavily in building the best creator platform with the best team in the creator economy and are looking for a Product Designer to support our mission.

This role is based in New York or San Francisco and open to those who are able to be in-office 2 days per week on a hybrid work model.

About The Team

We're hiring a Product Designer to join Creator Success, shaping the core experiences that help creators build sustainable businesses and engaged communities on Patreon. You'll design tools and touchpoints that help creators publish their work, attract and retain fans, and present their creative offerings in compelling ways. Your work will span how creators showcase their content, onboard to the platform, and grow their audiences, ensuring both free and paid experiences feel polished and purposeful.

You'll tackle high-impact problems across the creator journey. You'll design publishing workflows for podcasters, video creators, and newsletter writers. You'll shape how creators present their work to potential fans. And you'll build systems that help creators understand what to do next to succeed. This is a collaborative role where you'll partner closely with Product, Engineering, and Research to bring clarity to ambiguous opportunities and ship experiences that directly influence how hundreds of thousands of creators grow their businesses on Patreon.

- Proactively discover company-level opportunities and bring clarity and insight through high-fidelity prototypes and clear communication of design rationale to senior stakeholders and cross-functional partners

- Contribute to the visioning, sequencing, tactics, and execution of a multi-phased overhaul of the product
- Own, redefine, and ship key parts of the core Patreon product

title: Product Designer
description:
About The Company

Owner is an innovative, AI-native platform designed to empower local business owners, starting with restaurants, to succeed in the digital age. Our comprehensive system consolidates multiple tools—such as website management, online ordering, customer relationship management, and point-of-sale solutions—into a unified, intelligent platform that automates and streamlines daily operations. Our product philosophy centers on reducing the workload for small business owners by providing agentic tools that generate demand, convert leads, and facilitate business growth seamlessly. We aim to create a product experience that feels like having a dedicated team of operators, engineers, and marketers working on your behalf.

Founded with a vision to help independent restaurants thrive online, Owner is expanding its impact to other local business sectors facing similar challenges. We recognize that large technology corporations are encroaching on local markets, often eroding profits and customer bases. Our mission is to democratize access to powerful digital tools, enabling tens of millions of small business owners to compete effectively and sustain their livelihoods. Since 2020, Owner has generated tens of millions in revenue, processed over a billion dollars in online orders, and helped over 20,000 restaurant owners save nearly $200 million in fees. Our team comprises top talent from leading SMB software companies, and we operate as a remote-first, global organization headquartered in San Francisco, with a sales hub in Toronto.

About The Role

We are seeking a highly experienced and passionate Senior/Staff+ Product Designer to join our dynamic team. In this role, you will play a pivotal part in shaping the future of our platform by designing intuitive, scalable, and impactful user experiences. You will collaborate closely with engineering, product management, and leadership to drive product strategy and innovation. Your work will span from early exploration and prototyping to final implementation, with a focus on AI-powered features that enhance the customer journey. You will be responsible for advancing our design systems, maintaining high standards of clarity, simplicity, and usability, and ensuring that our products serve the needs of independent business owners effectively. This is a remote position, open to candidates across the US and Canada, with optional in-person collaboration opportunities at our San Francisco office.

Qualifications



- 7+ years of product design experience with a proven track record of leading complex, cross-functional projects
- Strong fundamentals in product and visual design, with meticulous attention to detail
- Experience collaborating closely with engineers, including prototyping in code and submitting pull requests
- Ability to navigate ambiguity and deliver results in a fast-paced environment
- Curiosity and confidence in designing with emerging technologies, including AI
- Excellent communication skil

title: Brand Designer, Iconography & Illustration - Instagram Brand Studio
description:
Instagram is seeking a designer to lead our icon and illustration programs. You'll own the holistic icon system and illustration style that billions of users interact with daily — creating new artwork, maintaining and refreshing our asset libraries, designing brand logos, and delivering guidance to cross-functional partners. You're a conceptual thinker who communicates big ideas in small spaces. You have a clear, informed perspective on iconography and illustration, and it shows in your work. You think systematically about how a brand icon system holds together — from the grid and stroke weight to the personality and meaning of each symbol. You will work independently but also collaborate closely with product designers, engineers, marketing, and product staff, providing art direction to other artists and designers.

Brand Designer, Iconography & Illustration - Instagram Brand Studio Responsibilities:



- Lead and maintain Instagram's iconography system — developing new icons, refreshing existing ones, and ensuring consistency across the full library
- Drive Instagram's Illustration and Iconography Intake program — fielding requests from cross-functional partners, prioritizing work, and delivering high-quality assets on schedule
- Define and evolve icon and illustration style guidelines, ensuring they align with Instagram's broader brand identity system
- Concept, iterate, polish, and deliver final icon and illustration assets in production-ready formats (Figma, SVG, Adobe Illustrator — live-stroke and expanded versions)
- Partner with product design and engineering teams to ship icons and illustrations in the product, ensuring assets work at all sizes and contexts
- Present design rationale and system-level decisions to stakeholders, building alignment and defending craft standards
- Identify opportunities to innovate on the icon/illustration system — improving efficiency, introducing new styles, or leveraging AI to accelerate production
- Provide art direction and mentorship to other illustrators and designers contributing to the icon system

Minimum Qualifications:



- 8+ years of experience in iconography, illustration, or visual design with a focus on systematic icon/illustration programs
- A portfolio showcasing high-quality icon systems, illustration work, and brand visual assets — demonstrating both systematic thinking and individual craft quality
- Proficiency in Adobe Illustrator, Figma, and vector-based design workflows
- Experience defining and scaling icon or illustration systems across large product ecosystems with multiple surfaces
- Demonstrated ability to work independently, manage multiple concurrent requests, and deliver production-ready assets with clean file organization
- Strong understanding of designing for constrained, space-limited product environments across platforms (iOS, Android, web)
- Experience presenting work clearly to stakeholders, inviting feedback, and iterating efficiently

title: Product Designer
description:
Midstream is an AI-native financial operating system for health systems, founded by experienced entrepreneurs and backed by top-tier investors. We give finance, supply chain, and managed care teams real-time visibility into where margin is at risk, with a precise action plan for capturing it before it's gone.

Purpose-built for healthcare's complexity, Midstream transforms structured, unstructured, and external data into instant, contract-aware insights that drive smarter decisions. Our AI agents unify spend and revenue operations across the full back-office, learning and adapting with every interaction and delivering always-on intelligence that no point solution or one-off engagement can match.

We're compressing months to minutes and turning post-period hindsight into in-the-moment foresight. The tempo of healthcare finance is changing, and Midstream is leading it.

Opportunity

Midstream is building the financial AI platform that helps health systems identify, validate, and realize millions of dollars in financial opportunities across supply chain, pharmacy, and managed care.

We're looking for a Product Designer who is excited to solve some of healthcare's most complex operational problems. You'll partner closely with Product, Engineering, Customer Success, and our health system partners to transform fragmented, manual workflows into intuitive, AI-powered experiences that help organizations make faster, better financial decisions.

This is a role for someone who loves owning product experiences from end to end. You'll help shape product strategy by understanding how customers work, uncovering opportunities through research, and translating complex enterprise workflows into intuitive, scalable experiences. You'll own the design process from discovery through launch and iteration, helping define how AI-native enterprise software should feel.

As our second designer, your primary focus will be building exceptional product experiences. At the same time, we're still an early-stage company where everyone contributes beyond the boundaries of their role when it creates the greatest impact. Whether supporting a product launch, improving customer-facing experiences, or helping communicate complex ideas more clearly, you'll bring a thoughtful design perspective wherever it helps move the company forward.

As one of the early designers at Midstream, you'll have the opportunity to shape not only the product, but how design contributes to the company as we scale.

What You'll Be Doing

Own end-to-end product design

Lead the complete design lifecycle—from customer research and problem definition to wireframes, prototypes, visual design, launch, and continuous iteration. Partner closely with Product and Engineering to deliver experiences that solve meaningful customer problems and create measurable business value.

Deeply understand our customers

Build a deep understanding of Midstream's business, our health system partners, and the operational challenges

About ThredUp

ThredUp is transforming resale with technology and a mission to inspire the world to think secondhand first. By making it easy to buy and sell secondhand, ThredUp has become one of the world's largest online resale platforms for apparel, shoes and accessories. Sellers love ThredUp because we make it easy to clean out their closets and unlock value for themselves or for the charity of their choice while doing good for the planet. Buyers love shopping value, premium and luxury brands all in one place, at up to 90% off estimated retail price. Our proprietary operating platform is the foundation for our managed marketplace and consists of distributed processing infrastructure, proprietary software and systems and data science expertise. With ThredUp’s Resale-as-a-Service, some of the world's leading brands and retailers are leveraging our platform to deliver customizable, scalable resale experiences to their customers. Recognized on TIME Most Influential Companies of 2023, Digiday's WorkLife 50 2023, TIME's Best Inventions of 2022, and Lattice's People Success Awards 2022.

About KREWE

KREWE is an independent, high-fashion eyewear brand rooted in the vibrant culture and boundless creativity of our hometown, New Orleans - and now proudly headquartered in both New Orleans and New York City. Since our launch in 2013, KREWE has grown into a dynamic brand celebrated for its distinctive, handcrafted sun and optical frames that reflect a deep commitment to quality, individuality, and design.

In 2022, we opened the doors to our NYC headquarters in the heart of the Meatpacking District, building a second home for the brand that brings New Orleans’ culture, creativity, and energy to one of the world’s most iconic design capitals. Our presence now spans brick-and-mortar boutiques, mobile retail concepts, and a thriving e-commerce platform - alongside distribution through premier independents and top national retailers. Celebrated for our unique approach to design, KREWE has cultivated a loyal following among style-conscious consumers and influential tastemakers.

As we continue to expand, we’re looking for passionate, driven, and innovative individuals to join our talented team. At KREWE our work is fast-paced, collaborative, and deeply mission-driven. Our people are high-performing and ambitious - not just about hitting goals, but about building something that’s original, culturally rooted and globally resonant. Every team member at KREWE has the opportunity to own their role and make a lasting impact. If this sounds like the right environment for you we invite you to apply below.

We are currently searching for a Junior Product Designer to expand the department’s design capacity while leading its understanding of future product, color, and trend opportunity. This individual will carry that point of view through product completion, coordinating input from across the design team rather than generating it alone. The Junior Product Designer will own non-frame development end to end including briefing, and the standing collaboration with Marketing on channel needs. This role reports to Senior Product Designer.

This role is based in our New Orleans Headquarters with periodic travel to New York.

- Supports the end-to-end design and development of new products, from concept through production.
- Researches trends, color, materials, and consumer insights to support the identification of future product opportunities.
- Develops seasonal color palettes and product concepts aligned with the brand's design direction.
- Owns the design and development of non-frame products, ensuring projects are delivered on time and to quality standards.
- Creates clear design briefs and coordinates cross-functional input throughout the product development process.
- Partners closely with Marketing to develop products that support campaign, merchandising, and channel needs.

title: Product Designer, Amazon Music Product Design
description:
Description

As a Product Designer on the Amazon Music Core Experiences Design team, you will design voice-first and multimodal interactions that shape how customers experience music through spoken language. You'll work at the intersection of visual craft and conversational design — crafting TTS responses, anticipating how customers interpret single and multi-turn voice interactions, and ensuring spoken experiences pair seamlessly with on-screen content across Alexa-enabled devices.

Working alongside senior product designers, product managers, engineers, and researchers, you will support the design of voice interactions that feel natural, useful, and delightful. You'll use your knowledge of conversational UX and visual design to build, iterate, and refine solutions with guidance from your team. To succeed, you need a passion for language, empathy for how people listen and respond, strong visual sensibilities, and the curiosity to explore how voice and screen work together.

Key job responsibilities



-  Design voice interactions and TTS response flows that are clear, natural, and contextually appropriate for Amazon Music customers
-  Create conversational wireframes, sample dialog scripts, response mapping documents, and flow diagrams to communicate design intent
-  Iterate on single-turn and multi-turn voice interaction patterns, anticipating how customers will interpret and respond to spoken prompts
-  Collaborate with design, product, engineering, and research teams to incorporate customer feedback, technical constraints, and usability findings into designs
-  Leverage existing templates and design systems to produce high-fidelity mockups for multimodal voice+screen experiences
-  Partner with cross-functional teams to ensure voice responses align with broader platform patterns
-  Present design work to partners and stakeholders for review and feedback
-  Contribute to language model training data and sample dialog interactions under guidance from senior designers

A day in the life

You'll start your day reviewing how a new TTS response sounds and reads on an Echo Show — does it feel rushed? Is the information hierarchy right when paired with the visual card? You'll sketch out a multi-turn flow for a new music request pattern, thinking through what happens when a customer says "no, not that one." You'll pair with your PM to walk through edge cases, sync with an engineer on what's technically feasible for response latency, and bring your work to a design crit where the team helps you refine the conversational cadence. You'll end the day documenting your iteration in Figma and noting open questions for research.

description:
Description

As a Product Designer on the Amazon Music Core Experiences Design team, you will design voice-first and multimodal interactions that shape how customers experience music through spoken language. You'll work at the intersection of visual craft and conversational design — crafting TTS responses, anticipating how customers interpret single and multi-turn voice interactions, and ensuring spoken experiences pair seamlessly with on-screen content across Alexa-enabled devices.

Working alongside senior product designers, product managers, engineers, and researchers, you will support the design of voice interactions that feel natural, useful, and delightful. You'll use your knowledge of conversational UX and visual design to build, iterate, and refine solutions with guidance from your team. To succeed, you need a passion for language, empathy for how people listen and respond, strong visual sensibilities, and the curiosity to explore how voice and screen work together.

Key job responsibilities



-  Design voice interactions and TTS response flows that are clear, natural, and contextually appropriate for Amazon Music customers
-  Create conversational wireframes, sample dialog scripts, response mapping documents, and flow diagrams to communicate design intent
-  Iterate on single-turn and multi-turn voice interaction patterns, anticipating how customers will interpret and respond to spoken prompts
-  Collaborate with design, product, engineering, and research teams to incorporate customer feedback, technical constraints, and usability findings into designs
-  Leverage existing templates and design systems to produce high-fidelity mockups for multimodal voice+screen experiences
-  Partner with cross-functional teams to ensure voice responses align with broader platform patterns
-  Present design work to partners and stakeholders for review and feedback
-  Contribute to language model training data and sample dialog interactions under guidance from senior designers

A day in the life

You'll start your day reviewing how a new TTS response sounds and reads on an Echo Show — does it feel rushed? Is the information hierarchy right when paired with the visual card? You'll sketch out a multi-turn flow for a new music request pattern, thinking through what happens when a customer says "no, not that one." You'll pair with your PM to walk through edge cases, sync with an engineer on what's technically feasible for response latency, and bring your work to a design crit where the team helps you refine the conversational cadence. You'll end the day documenting your iteration in Figma and noting open questions for research.

Amazon Music is an immersive audio entertainment service that deepens connections between fans, artists, and creators. title: Product Designer
description:
About The Role

We're looking for a product designer who wants to operate like a founder.

Not someone who waits for tickets or perfect requirements. Someone who sees opportunities, prototypes fast, shapes product direction, and ships experiences that move the company forward.

This is not a "make the UI pretty" role. You'll work across product thinking, interaction design, systems, prototyping, and execution. In many cases, you'll go from idea → prototype → shipped product in days, not quarters.

The best people for this role think strategically, build relentlessly, and use AI as leverage.

Why This Role Is Different

The role of design is changing.

AI has collapsed the distance between idea and execution. The best designers today don't just create mockups, they can explore product directions, prototype interactions, generate working interfaces, and pressure-test ideas themselves.

We Believe The Future Belongs To Designers Who



- Think like product leaders
- Prototype like engineers
- Use AI tools fluently
- Care about outcomes, not deliverables
- Move from ambiguity to shipped product with very little overhead

If that excites you, you'll probably love working here.

What You'll Work On



- Own product areas end-to-end, from initial insight to shipped experience
- Lead greenfield explorations and turn blank-canvas ideas into real products
- Prototype aggressively, in code, AI tools, Figma, or whatever gets the idea across fastest
- Work directly with engineers and PMs to shape product direction, not just execution
- Think deeply about systems, workflows, and how features compound across the platform
- Use AI tools as part of your daily workflow to increase speed, creativity, and iteration velocity
- Raise the quality bar across the company through strong product judgment and craft
- Push ideas into reality quickly instead of over-optimizing in planning phases

How We Work



- We optimize for speed of learning and iteration
- We prototype early instead of debating endlessly
- We use AI heavily across design, product thinking, research, and engineering
- We believe small, high-agency teams can outperform much larger organizations
- We believe the best builders in the AI era are token maxxers, people who use AI relentlessly to compress execution cycles, test ideas faster, and expand the scope of what a single person can accomplish
- We care more about shipping and learning than rigid role boundaries

What We're Looking For



- 3–6 years of product design experience, ideally at startups or highly product-driven teams
- A strong track record of owning products or features from concept through launch
- High agency. You naturally move things forward without waiting for direction
- Strong product instincts and clear opinions about what should exist and why

About Flint

The best education anyone has ever received is one person paying close attention to one student: moving at their pace, noticing what they missed, asking the next question at the right moment. But the current system is built around a compromise with one teacher managing thirty students.

Flint exists to take that compromise off the table. Personalized learning, at the scale of a whole school — every student working with something closer to a tutor, and every teacher able to see what's actually happening across their class instead of guessing.

Go look at the product before you read any further: app.flintk12.com

The Role

Students want something that stays with them, going at their pace and helps them get unstuck without just handing over the answer. Teachers want that happening inside a class they still control, and they'd like their evenings back. Admins want proof that the platform they rolled out is leading to teacher productivity and student progress.

Your job is to dive deep into this design problem, holding three sets of needs within one product. We’ll trust you to ship designs that are the best possible solution to our users most urgent pain points. tl;dr you'll get to own how Flint works and how it feels.

How We Work



- We move fast, and closely. You'll work with a small, senior team: one Product Lead, a Chief of Staff (Product), a CTO, and five engineers. We also have a running joke that we can’t keep up with our #product_updates channel because of how much we ship.
- Fast and good aren't in tension here. In our experience the fastest route to something good is getting a rough version in front of a real teacher early, which tends to be quicker than getting it right in private. Decisions with the highest impact have often happened within days, not month long sprints.
- We’re always learning. Call it on-brand or a bit on the nose, but learning from each other, our customers, the market have been key to our growth. We even have channels dedicated to sharing our workflow mistakes and wins. Education is also still being actively shaped as a field, and staying tuned to what users and the industry are telling us matters more than assuming we already know.
- Users drive our decisions. Our team isn't exclusively made up of former teachers, and that's deliberate. We'd rather build from real user feedback and a range of perspectives than from any one person's classroom experience. Our close connection with teachers, students, and admins helps us quickly understand what's working and what isn't.
- We design with AI, not around it. Lo-fi concepts out of Claude, prototypes we can put in front of a teacher the same week, PRDs drafted from screenshots and voice notes: these are just a few ways we’ve used AI to support our work, and it's a real part of why our loop is as short as it is.

title: Product Designer
description:
In the 1960s, the Italian artist and inventor Bruno Munari was studying spontaneous forms: shapes that emerge from the interaction of material, function, and environment.

When Danese Milano commissioned him to design a lamp that was practical, durable, affordable, and easy to transport, Munari was reminded of the traditional rice paper lanterns he had encountered when traveling in Japan. But rice paper lanterns are fragile, hard to clean, and tend to yellow over time.

Looking for an industrial alternative, he discovered filanca—a synthetic stretch nylon used exclusively for women's stockings at the time.

Munari visited hosiery factories to test the material and see what forms it could take. "We do not make lamps, sir. Only stockings," one factory told him. Munari replied, "You'll see."

The result was the Falkland lamp: only a few centimeters thick when packaged, as tall as a human when hung, its spontaneous form emerging from the elasticity of the nylon and metal rings of different diameters inserted at regular intervals, enlarged by gravity when suspended from above.

Munari didn't begin with the form of a lamp. He began with the qualities it needed, then looked outside the conventions of lighting to find the right materials and methods. We're looking for a designer who works the same way: someone who studies the systems and materials at hand, then finds a way of putting them together that feels both unexpected and inevitable.

At Co–Star, the materials are a 4,000-year-old system of astrology, planetary data from NASA, and a corpus written by astrologers and poets. The qualities we're designing for: astrology made accessible without asking anyone to learn a complex system, and a language that lets people share something intimate with their friends.

We're hiring a Senior Product Designer to continue cultivating those qualities across Co–Star and new experiments. You'll move between product architecture, interaction design, prototyping, and visual design. Ideas rarely arrive as polished specs. You'll help decide what we make next and how it works.

title: Product Designer I
description:
ICON is hiring a UX professional to own the user experience for a core product area within BuildOS - our software platform used by architects, builders, and construction operators. In this role, you will lead end-to-end UX work for tools that connect users to ICON's construction technology, from discovery research through design handoff. You will run customer interviews, map complex workflows, build prototypes, test them with real users, and write specs that engineering can build from. You will work alongside engineers, product leadership, and internal and external customers to shape what gets built and why. This role is based at ICON's Austin, TX office and reports to the Director of Product.


RESPONSIBILITIES:
Discovery and Research: Run regular interviews with architects, engineers, and builders to learn their workflows, pain points, and unmet needs. Document assumptions, evidence gaps, and research priorities for your product area. Turn findings into clear insights that shape the roadmap.
Workflow Mapping and UX Design: Map user workflows and edge cases for complex, multi-step construction and design processes. Design for a range of users, from technical specialists to first-time operators with different levels of software fluency. Define data needs, integration points, and error states.
Wireframes and Prototypes: Create wireframes, interaction flows, and interactive prototypes in Figma or a similar tool. Deliver designs that are functional, polished, and clear.
Prototyping and Usability Testing: Build and test prototypes with target users on a regular cadence. Run lightweight usability tests and update designs based on real feedback. Check designs with engineering for technical feasibility before handoff.
Handoff and Engineering Collaboration: Deliver developer-ready specs with annotated designs, acceptance criteria, and interaction details. Work two or more sprints ahead of engineering so teams always have clear, well-defined work to pick up.
Cross-Functional Partnership: Collaborate daily with engineers, product leadership, and cross-functional partners. Present design choices to engineers, leaders, and customers in plain terms.
Strategic Alignment: Connect your design work to company-wide Objectives and Key Results (OKRs) so the user experience moves bigger goals forward.
MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS:

- 3+ in UX design, product design, or a similar role.
- A portfolio showing end-to-end design work — research through shipped product, not visual design alone.
- Experience running user interviews and turning qualitative research into design decisions.
- Strong fluency with Figma or a similar tool for wireframing, prototyping, and design systems.
- Experience designing for workflows with real constraints, not only consumer apps.
- Clear communication skills. You can explain design choices to engineers, leaders, and customers.
- Comfort working through ambiguity. You can define the problem, not just solve a defined one.

SyntheticFi is a fast-growing FinTech startup redefining the securities-backed lending world. We partner via B2B channels with Registered Investment Advisors (RIAs). Through our product, clients of RIAs are able to access the SPX box spread market, an institutional source of liquidity.

Cape is America’s privacy-first mobile carrier. Our mission is to be a force for good in global wireless. Cape was founded in 2022 by people who believe privacy is a fundamental right, not a luxury to be traded away. Our journey began when our founder recognized a critical vulnerability in our modern world: everyone relies on the same stagnant cellular infrastructure and legacy systems that track our every movement, monitor and profile our connections, and lose and sell our personal data.

Product Designer at Lumion
Location: In-office, South Jordan, Utah Comp: Salary, meaningful equity, and bonuses tied to company revenue


What Lumion does
Lumion is the all-in-one operating system for trade and technical schools. We power the entire institution: AI-driven lead generation and conversion, enrollment, financial aid, student lifecycle management, and tuition payments. Most schools are still stitching together five or six disconnected tools to do what our platform handles.


America has a massive skilled trades shortage and the schools that train electricians, welders, and nurses are the bottleneck. We're backed by TTV Capital and Tusk Venture Partners.
Why this role matters


You would be Lumion's first dedicated product designer. Until now, design has been done by the founders, product managers, and engineers. That carried us a long way, and it is no longer enough.


Our engineers build with AI-native workflows, so the constraint on the product is no longer how fast we can write code. It is how fast we can figure out exactly what to build and make it excellent. That is design work, and right now it is our bottleneck.


The people who use our platform are admissions directors, school owners, and finance staff who live in it all day, and students making one of the bigger financial decisions of their lives. Most software in this industry was built a decade ago and looks like it. You get to set the bar for what great looks like in this market.


The work
You will own design across the entire platform.


Product design end to end. You take features from PRD to shipped: user flows, interaction design, high-fidelity UI, and specs engineers can build from without guessing. You will work directly with the CEO and CTO in design sessions and own the outcome.


Prototypes. Before engineering commits to a build, we want a working prototype in front of real schools. You will produce clickable, testable prototypes fast and use what you learn to sharpen the spec before a line of production code gets written.


The design system. The platform spans lead management, enrollment, messaging, scheduling, payments, and reporting, and it grew fast. You will build the component library and interaction patterns that make it feel like one product, and that let engineers ship good UI without a designer in the room.


AI interfaces. Schools use Lumion to configure and supervise AI agents that text, email, and call prospective students. Designing how a non-technical admissions director sets up an agent, reviews its conversations, and learns to trust it is new territory with little prior art. You will define those patterns.


Student surfaces. Enrollment applications, document signing, and tuition payments, mostly on a phone. These flows handle real money and real decisions, and they have to be effortless.

title: Product Designer
description:
About Fluidstack

We exist to make humanity more free. For most of human history, you farmed or you starved. Technology gave people more time for the things they wanted to do, instead of things they had to do. Powerful AI will be the biggest lever for human choice we've ever built - but only if models are aligned with what humanity actually wants. There are groups building AI who don't share these goals. Whoever deploys frontier compute infrastructure fastest will decide whether AI expands human freedom or shrinks it.

We're singularly focused on delivering 10 to 100s of GWs of compute faster than anyone else, rethinking every layer of the stack. We acquire power, design and build data centers, and operate them - with teams spanning hardware and software. Speed and scale are our key differentiators. Come be a part of building civilization-scale infrastructure for AI.

We hire people who care deeply about this problem space. If that is you, please apply!

About The Role

Fluidstack is looking for a Product Designer who can own the end-to-end design of our products, both internal and external, from the first sketch to the last pixel shipped. This is a hands-on IC role, not a design strategy or oversight position. You will be the designer embedded with our product and engineering teams, shaping the interfaces that GPU cluster operators, AI platform engineers, and enterprise infrastructure teams interact with every day.

Our products are deeply technical and our developers and team members are power users, they are engineers and operators who work in terminals, read documentation compulsively, and have zero tolerance for UX that wastes their time. Designing for them requires genuine fluency in developer tools, infrastructure dashboards, and complex, data-dense interfaces. You need to know what great looks like in this space and be able to build it yourself.

You will work directly with PMs and engineers, as well as our customers, own design end-to-end for your product areas, and bring a strong visual sensibility that elevates everything you touch. - Own design end-to-end across research, wireframes, high-fidelity mockups, prototypes, and shipped production UI.

- Build and maintain a coherent design system: components and interaction patterns that scale across a growing product surface area.

Whatnot is the largest live shopping platform in North America and Europe to buy, sell, and discover the things you love. Whether it's trading cards, fashion, electronics, or live plants, our sellers are building real businesses across hundreds of categories. Every year, we sponsor 2 remote UX apprentices from anywhere in the world to join us for 7 months, either in the fall or spring seasons or online. title: Visual Designer, Product
description:
You'll own the visual quality of Luma's product: the typography, color, iconography, spacing, and components that make it feel exceptional, and the design system that lets the whole team hold that bar as the product grows. This is a craft-first role with a strong point of view.

It isn't a redesign-everything role. You're elevating what exists and building the scalable foundation underneath it, including a living design system engineers and designers actually reference when they build. It fits someone who thinks in systems and can defend why a decision is right, not just how it looks. If you prefer one-off screens over a coherent system, this won't suit.

What You'll Own

- Set and hold the visual bar, establishing what good looks like and advocating for it across the product.
- Shape how new features look before they're built, bringing a visual perspective to early concepting.

First 90 Days

One way the first 90 could unfold.



- Days 1–30 — Immerse & Diagnose: Audit the product's visual quality and map where it falls short and what the design system needs.
- Days 30–60 — Ship & Validate: Elevate a high-visibility surface and stand up the first version of the systematized visual language in Figma.
- Days 60–90 — Scale & Systemize: Build the live, interactive design system the team uses when shipping new features.

What You Bring



- 7+ years in visual and UI design, with a portfolio showing exceptional craft across typography, color, layout, and interaction.
- Systems thinking: you turn a strong visual language into a scalable, consistent foundation.
- Experience building or significantly contributing to a design system a team actually uses.
- You build with AI coding tools to produce real outputs, not just mockups, and iterate until they meet your bar.
- A clear point of view you can articulate, and a portfolio of work that shipped and improved product quality.
- A portfolio showing design-systems experience is required.

Nice to Have



- Experience building a token system from scratch and connecting it to a live codebase.
- Experience building a live component library or design system with AI coding tools.
- Experience designing for desktop applications (our product is desktop-first).

About Luma: Luma's mission is to build unified general intelligence that can generate, understand, and operate in the physical world. We believe multimodality is critical for intelligence — the next step beyond language models comes from vision. Luma is an equal opportunity employer.

About Us

Our mission is to reinvent the way people learn, starting with language.

Learning a language can change a life by opening doors to new cultures, careers, and communities. Two billion people around the world are actively trying to learn a language, but the best way to learn (one-on-one tutoring) is hard to access at scale and hasn’t been meaningfully improved in decades. Speak is building a human-level, AI-powered tutor in your pocket: a conversation-first experience that lets learners actually speak, get instant feedback, and progress through carefully designed lessons. The result is a complete path from beginner to confident speaker across multiple languages.

Speak first launched in South Korea in 2019, where Speak has now become the number one language learning app, and we now serve learners across many markets and 15+ languages. Speak is one of the world’s leading AI companies, with over $150m raised in venture investment from OpenAI, Accel, Founders Fund, Khosla Ventures, and more, with a distributed team across San Francisco, Seoul, Tokyo, Taipei, and Ljubljana.

About The Design Team

We’re a small, high-craft team that sits at the intersection of research, invention, and product thinking. We build consumer and B2B experiences used by millions across 150+ markets — and a lot of the work is genuinely novel: inventing how someone talks to an AI tutor, what feedback feels like when you’re learning out loud, and how progress should be measured and celebrated.

About Agora Intelligence (d.b.a. Tilt)
Agora Intelligence is building the audited methodology layer agents call before touching portfolios. Our product, Tilt, is GitHub for rules-based investment methodologies: an open platform and marketplace where investment strategies are created, tested, audited, and distributed — by humans and AI agents alike. As AI agents begin managing real portfolios, they need a trusted source of verified investment logic before they can act. Tilt is that source.
We operate across two connected surfaces: InvestOS, an open standard that lets any brokerage or platform plug verified methodology into its own AI experience; and Tilt, the reference implementation of InvestOS. Tilt is an agentic harness where investors, portfolio managers, and creators can author, remix, and publish strategies. We're a small, senior team (from BlackRock, Bloomberg, BGI, and Quant Funds) backed by Portage Ventures, Lerer Hippeau, Cumberland Investments (and more), working with major brokerages and financial data providers.


What We're Building
InvestOS — an open standard for rules-based methodologies and its reference implementation.
We believe any idea — a theme, a trend, a thesis — can be turned into an investable view. On Tilt, anyone can express a view as a rules-based basket of assets in seconds, backed by evidence and scored against what actually happens. Whether you're modeling a thematic strategy, tracking an emerging technology, or capturing the public-market footprint of a private company, what used to take an index committee months now takes an API call — 100× faster, at a fraction of the cost. We also transform views found on the open web, into rules-based strategies. This lets us measure the performance of any opinion or prediction about the future. The unit is a tilt: a creator-authored view of the world.


The bigger bet: as AI agents take on more of investing, they'll need an open, trusted standard for how investment views are expressed, verified, and combined. When anyone can generate a strategy in seconds, the strategies aren't the asset. The system that versions, tests, and grades them is. We're building that standard — and the platform where those views are made. We’re also building the learning loops for when views resolve against reality, as measured by markets.


Who We Are
We're a team of ~25 senior-to-principal engineers, designers and AI/ML researchers. More than half the team are former founders. We move fast, challenge assumptions, and believe AI should fundamentally change how financial products are built. We have no management hierarchy and work remotely with 4 one-week hackathons per year. “Full stack” to us means you own a slice of the product, including its roadmap and go-to-market.

title: Staff Product Designer
description:
Staff Product Designer


Remote (US) · Full-time
Lead product design for VA.gov services that help Veterans get the benefits and care they have earned. Remote across the United States.


About the role
Selara is hiring a Staff Product Designer to work on VA.gov, the digital front door for the Department of Veterans Affairs. The services you design reach millions of Veterans who use VA.gov to apply for benefits, manage their health care, and track their claims. Good design here is not decoration. It is the difference between a Veteran finishing an application and giving up on it.
This is a staff level role. You will ship product design on a cross-functional team and raise the design bar well beyond your own work.


What you'll do

- Own product design for VA.gov experiences end to end, from discovery and research through shipped, measured outcomes
- Plan and run research with Veterans and VA staff, then turn findings into decisions the whole team can act on
- Design within the VA Design System and contribute improvements back to it, so every experience stays consistent with the rest of VA.gov
- Design form-heavy, high-stakes flows in plain language that people can complete under stress
- Treat accessibility as a first-class design constraint and deliver work that meets WCAG 2.1 AA and Section 508 from the first draft, not as a cleanup pass
- Work shoulder to shoulder with engineers, iterating in staging and reviewing built work against design intent
- Set design standards, mentor designers and teammates in user-centered practice, and represent design in program-level reviews


What we're looking for

- Significant product design experience, typically eight or more years across research, interaction design, visual design, and content design
- A portfolio of shipped, complex services, ideally forms, eligibility flows, or other transactional experiences rather than marketing surfaces
- Hands-on research skill, including usability testing, synthesis, and the judgment to pick lightweight methods that fit the moment
- Deep working knowledge of accessible design practice and experience shipping to WCAG and Section 508 standards
- Fluency working inside a mature design system and the judgment to know when to extend it
- Strong facilitation, writing, and mentoring skills in a remote, distributed team
- The ability to influence product direction through partnership rather than authority


Nice to have

- Experience designing for VA.gov, another federal agency, or regulated industries like health care
- Familiarity with the US Web Design System or the VA Design System
- Experience with government design review cycles such as design intent and staging reviews
- Comfort reading and lightly prototyping in HTML and CSS


Location and eligibility
This role is fully remote within the United States. Work on VA.gov requires the ability to obtain and maintain a federal Public Trust suitability determination, which includes a background investigation.

The Production Graphic Designer Contractor will assist the NB Global Creative Studio team with production of global and regional digital marketing kits. This teammate must be an organized, dependable individual who is great at collaboration, communication, and needs to be able to multi-task overlapping projects while staying on deadlines. The candidate will be taking creative direction & feedback often, from several teammates, quick and efficient turnaround will be expected. Ideal candidate would be creative, flexible, self-directed and a problem solver with attention to detail, used to working in a busy design department. This is truly a production job - there will not be a lot of original artwork created. Friendliness, no ego, and grace under pressure are soft skills that are a must for this position.

This is a temporary 6-month contract position. The individual in this role will work a hybrid schedule, with three days per week on-site at our headquarters in Brighton, MA (Tuesday through Thursday) and two days per week remotely.

MAJOR ACCOUNTABILITIES:



- Under the direction of Lead Designers, Team Manager, or the Creative Director, the Jr. Production Graphic Designer will execute a variety of creative projects (for example, global and regional emails, site components, social, affiliate banners, OOH and occasionally print advertising). 
- They will be expected to handle several projects at a time and keep the Lead Designer & Global Ops Coordinator informed of any issues that may arise. Keeping a high level of creative output while holding to deadlines is a must. 

REQUIREMENTS FOR SUCCESS:



- Bachelor degree in design, 2+ years work experience creating and designing special projects. Proven knowledge and success in working across a variety of formats. 
- In addition to design, typical duties include routing creative for approvals, following up often to keep deadlines on track, preparing, and uploading final working files to our DAM system. 
- This person should have advanced knowledge of Figma, Illustrator, InDesign and Photoshop. 
- Prior experience working in a project workflow management app such as Asana or ProWorkflow is preferred. 

Decision-Making Authority:

The Production Graphic Designer candidate will get direction from a Lead Designer and does not have the authority to make decisions on artwork. Keeping consistent with Brand Guidelines is a must. Any artwork created during their time at New Balance is property of New Balance.
